---
title: "Eigenmode and Offline EPR"
---

::: {.callout-note title="CONVERGING candidate contract"}
Both backends provide one solver-specific `EigenmodeSim` with surface, bulk,
and port/junction EPR analysis. Their preparation and result types remain
backend-owned. Offline film reanalysis uses recorded result evidence and does
not reopen a solver. This page documents the current candidate; it does not
claim V1 stability. The [Backend Support Matrix](backend-support.qmd) separates
the implemented candidate from the currently documented exercise evidence and
limits.
:::

## Workflow and state contract

| Step | AEDT | Palace |
|---|---|---|
| Configure | `scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim`: `set_geometry(component_or_geometry_input)`, `set_stack(mapping_or_json_path)`, `set_output_dir(path)`, `set_eigenmode(*, project_name, design_name, run_control, route='B', route_a_profile=None, resources=None, geometry_workers=None)`, `set_surface_epr(*, contributions=(), defaults=None)`, `add_junction(PlanarJunction)`, and `set_epr_request(EprAnalysisRequest | None)` | `scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim`: `set_geometry(component)`, `set_stack(mapping_or_json_path)`, `set_output_dir(path)`, `set_vacuum_region(...)`, `set_eigenmode(*, num_modes=10, target=None, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)`, and `set_mesh(*, refined_mesh_size, max_mesh_size)`. Optional EPR setup: `set_surface_epr(*, representation, specs, route_a_thin_film=None)`, `add_port(name, *, layer, layout_sheet=True, inductance)`, and `set_epr_request(*, surface_interfaces: Sequence[str] | None = None, bulk_domain_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None, port_names: Sequence[str] | None = None)`. |
| Prepare a handoff | `prepare_handoff()` creates the versioned HFSS Eigenmode package. It does not run HFSS. | `mesh()` creates the local mesh; `write_config()` writes Palace configuration; `prepare_handoff(*, profile, executable, resources=None, setup_commands=(), petsc_options=())` creates the manual run package. Quarto examples are disabled and do not call these methods. |
| Resolve returned results | `sim.resolve_results(run_dir=None)` resolves the AEDT run summary. `scgsim.aedt.resolve_epr_result(path)` loads the EPR result record. | `scgsim.palace.resolve_palace_result(run_dir, *, expected_handoff_id)` resolves a returned run; `resolved.epr_result()` detaches its final Eigenmode EPR quantities. `scgsim.palace.resolve_epr_result(path)` loads a detached EPR JSON file without reading the full solver run. |
| Reanalyze and show | `scgsim.aedt.reanalyze_epr(result, *, surface_defaults=None, group_overrides=None)` returns a fresh `EprResult`; `show_epr(result, *, mode=None, native_pass=None)` returns a Plotly `Figure`. | `scgsim.palace.reanalyze_epr(result, *, surface_defaults=None, group_overrides=None)` returns a fresh `PalaceEprResult`; `show_epr(result, *, mode=None)` returns a Plotly `Figure`. |

The ordinary Palace path prepares and resolves Eigenmode and domain-energy
results without surface specs, a lumped port, or an EPR request. Those inputs
are optional EPR declarations, not requirements for an Eigenmode run.

The result belongs to its backend: AEDT keeps an `EprResult` anchored to its
source evidence, while Palace can detach a `PalaceEprResult` with
`to_payload()` / `from_payload()`. Neither backend uses a shared simulation
base class. AEDT's `EprAnalysisRequest` is AEDT-specific; it is not a Palace
configuration object.

An ordinary Palace Eigenmode configuration does not need Surface-EPR specs or
a lumped port. Add `set_surface_epr()` and `add_port()` only for those EPR
model elements. Palace's
`set_epr_request(*, surface_interfaces: Sequence[str] | None = None, bulk_domain_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None, port_names: Sequence[str] | None = None)`
filters configured outputs. Surface values are `MA`, `MS`, and `SA`; bulk IDs
are SGB solution-volume `entry_name` values from `Domains.Postprocessing.Energy`;
port values are configured `LayoutPortBinding.name` values. `None` selects all
configured entries, `()` selects none, and an explicit subset must resolve.
Unknown selections fail against the exact index during config writing and
result extraction. The selection is retained in result-bound metadata and can
be read without a `Sim` object. It does not remove physical domains or ports
from the native model or change the normalization; ordinary Palace Eigenmode
also works without surface specs or ports.

AEDT's `EprAnalysisRequest` has `mode_indices`, `surface_contribution_ids`,
`junction_ids`, and `bulk_domain_ids`. `mode_indices=None` selects all requested
Eigenmodes; an explicit mode selection must be nonempty and valid. For each of
`surface_contribution_ids`, `junction_ids`, and `bulk_domain_ids`, `None` means
all supported configured entries, an empty tuple means none, and an explicit
selection must resolve. Omitting the AEDT EPR request means no EPR analysis
request.

## Quantities and normalization

The reported participation for a supported energy numerator is

$$
p_i = \frac{U_i}{U_{norm}}.
$$

AEDT uses the unique electric-domain normalization
$U_E=\epsilon_0/2\sum_D\int_D\epsilon_r|E|^2dV$ plus the declared
junction capacitive energies, $U_{norm}=U_E+\sum_j U_{C,j}$. Palace uses
its final native electric-domain and capacitive-energy tables for its
normalization. Thin-film estimates are numerator estimates; SCGSim does not add
them back into either backend's denominator. The detailed AEDT MA/MS/SA
surface formulas, material-side binding, and linearized junction normalization
are documented in [the AEDT Eigenmode reference](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization).

AEDT bulk domain participation uses
$U_D=\epsilon_0/2\int_D\epsilon_r|E|^2dV$ divided by the same denominator.
The report presents surface, bulk, and junction/port partitions on separate
axes; these views do not assert that every physical loss channel has been
evaluated.

For an AEDT planar junction, the source declaration includes its polygon,
terminal nets A and B, directed in-plane unit vector, width, inductance, and
capacitance. The formal area-average voltage and nonnegative inductive and
capacitive participation follow the convention in the linked reference.
Palace's `layout_sheet=True` port is a separate backend contract: it binds an
authored component port to a layer and inductance, then reports Palace's signed
native port participation. The signed value is phase-convention dependent and
is not the same quantity as AEDT's nonnegative $p_L$ or $p_C$.

## Surface identity, masks, and loss assumptions

For AEDT, each `SurfaceEprSpec` binds one contribution ID and source polygon ID
to an interface (`MA`, `MS`, or `SA`), a top/bottom field side, film thickness,
film permittivity, optional loss tangent, source, preset, and alternative mask
margins. `MA` means metal-air, `MS` metal-substrate, and `SA` substrate-air.
The `field_side` records the requested top/bottom side, and the adjacent source
domains and physical owner remain explicit evidence; none is inferred from a
display label. AEDT binds a native material side using its normal-based rule.
Its `effective_domain_id` remains binding metadata rather than a solver-domain
restriction or proof that the selected field belongs to that material. `MM`
may remain semantic evidence but is not a dielectric-film energy contribution.
Surface construction requires thickness and permittivity for MA/MS/SA. At
initial AEDT configuration, interface defaults fill unspecified optional loss
and provenance fields on valid contributions; explicit per-contribution
values, including an explicit zero loss tangent, take precedence. Defaults
cannot make an incomplete spec valid.

AEDT Surface EPR integrates horizontal top/bottom support only. It does not
calculate sidewall film energy. Its unmasked baseline and every requested
margin are separate evaluations; even a caller's explicit zero margin is a
separate row. Margins are alternatives, not additive bands. Empty physical
intersection is recorded as a geometric zero. Palace retains its native
surface and mask identities; when sidewalls were not selected, their energy
remains uncomputed rather than zero.

Film loss conversion is $Q^{-1}_i=p_i\tan\delta_i$. A missing loss tangent
means unknown and yields an unavailable inverse-Q contribution; an explicit
`0.0` is a known zero and yields a zero contribution. Offline reanalysis applies
partial updates in this order: recorded assumptions, interface defaults, then
group overrides. A later value replaces only the same field; an explicit
`None` loss update marks it unknown, while omitted fields retain their current
values. Group overrides target exact recorded group IDs and unknown IDs fail.
Reanalysis never selects contribution patches or changes the underlying
geometry or field evidence.

Palace's native configuration writes `LossTan=0.0` when the user did not
provide a loss tangent because that is the backend-compatible config value.
That native value does not turn an unknown assumption into a known zero: the
Palace v2 index and detached EPR result preserve `loss_tangent=None`, and
SCGSim's analysis keeps the inverse-Q contribution unavailable. A native
infinite-Q or zero-loss display is not evidence that the loss is known to be
zero.

Historical Palace surface-film records before
`scgsim.palace.surface-film.v2` can contain a recorded `loss_tangent=0.0`
whose origin is ambiguous. SCGSim retains that raw value in
`recorded_native_assumptions`, but treats the effective loss tangent as unknown
and marks its provenance `historical_ambiguous_zero`. Detached EPR results
preserve both the recorded value and that interpretation; the inverse-Q
contribution remains unavailable.

The `show_epr` figure layout, owner labels, coverage counts, and baseline
inverse-Q subtotal are specified in the [Unified Report Model](report-model.qmd#eigenmode-epr-presentation).
The subtotal is not total device loss or a lifetime estimate; requested mask
rows are alternatives and are not added into it. Sidewall terms remain
uncomputed where they were not evaluated.

## Static component examples

The paired examples use the public OrPen SC PDK Xmon component, which carries
structured conductor and topology annotations and an authored
`o_junction_lumped` port. The exact component dimensions, coupon padding and
clearance, port inductance, and preset names below come from the pinned public
[Palace Route B Eigenmode notebook](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon/palace_route_b_eigenmode.qmd)
and the same revision's public [component source](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/orpen_sc_pdk/cells/qubit.py)
and [preset records](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/orpen_sc_pdk/materials.json).
The imported layer stack, material records, and vacuum-padding constant are
defined in the same revision's public [technology source](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/orpen_sc_pdk/tech.py)
and [material helpers](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/orpen_sc_pdk/materials.py).
The package revision is
[`50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264)
(`orpen-sc-pdk==0.1.0`), with Python 3.12–3.13 and GDSFactory 9.48.x.
The public dependency constraints are in the pinned
[`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/pyproject.toml).
The PDK's literature-central film presets are modeling assumptions, not
measured material properties.

This common input builds the actual annotated component and corresponding
stack used by both backend snippets:

```python
import gdsfactory as gf
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk import LAYER_STACK, get_material_records
from orpen_sc_pdk.helpers.assembly import place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps
from scgsim.sgb import build_component_stack

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
component = gf.get_component(
    "kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit",
    bump_ring_count_per_side=0,
    qubit_pad_length=309.5,
    qubit_pad_width=24.65,
    qubit_gap=20.0,
)
coupon = place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps(
    component,
    coupon_padding_um=75.0,
    clearance_um=30.0,
    placement_mode="corner_anchors",
)
component = coupon.component
stack = build_component_stack(
    component=component,
    layer_stack=LAYER_STACK,
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=coupon.stack_coupon_padding_um,
)
```

### Palace Route B

The public component exposes `o_junction_lumped` on `D1_BOTTOM_M1`. This
static setup uses the PDK's validated literature-central MA/MS/SA presets and
the authored port as a Palace lumped port:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from orpen_sc_pdk import (
    get_interface_preset_records,
    validate_interface_preset_records,
)
from orpen_sc_pdk.tech import OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM
from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim

records = validate_interface_preset_records(get_interface_preset_records())
names = {"MA": "LiteratureCentral_MA", "MS": "LiteratureCentral_MS", "SA": "LiteratureCentral_SA"}
selected = {kind: records[name] for kind, name in names.items()}
epr_specs = {}
for kind, name in names.items():
    record = selected[kind]
    epr_specs[kind] = {
        "thickness": record["thickness"],
        "permittivity": record["permittivity"],
        "loss_tangent": record["loss_tangent"],
        "source": record["source"],
        "preset": name,
    }

sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_geometry(component)
sim.set_stack(stack)
sim.set_output_dir(Path("artifacts/palace-xmon-eigenmode"))
sim.set_vacuum_region(
    padding=(0.0, 0.0, float(OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM))
)
sim.set_surface_epr(representation="B", specs=epr_specs)
sim.add_port(
    "o_junction_lumped",
    layer="D1_BOTTOM_M1",
    layout_sheet=True,
    inductance=11.78e-9,
)
sim.set_eigenmode(num_modes=2, target=2e9, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)
sim.set_epr_request(
    surface_interfaces=("MA", "MS", "SA"),
    bulk_domain_ids=None,
    port_names=("o_junction_lumped",),
)
```

The [pinned public Palace notebook](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon/palace_route_b_eigenmode.qmd)
continues with explicit mesh controls, config generation, and a locally
configured manual-handoff profile. Those steps are deliberately not run by
this documentation build. Use a new, unused relative output directory for
each prepared handoff.

### AEDT HFSS Eigenmode

The same component and stack can enter the AEDT facade. Surface contributions
must use real IDs and polygon IDs from the prepared geometry's
`contribution_catalog`; the [catalogue-driven handoff example](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#catalogue-driven-handoff)
shows how to validate those selections before creating complete
`SurfaceEprSpec` records. No PDK-specific AEDT contribution ID is guessed
here. This example requests only bulk-domain outputs. The Eigenmode run-control
numbers below follow the public
[AEDT Eigenmode notebook](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/50b59e6e44953a5c6b5d760c3c496cb4c2f31264/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_eigenmode.py)
at the same pinned PDK revision; that file is cited for run-control values,
not for its distinct example geometry.

```python
from pathlib import Path

from scgsim.aedt import (
    EigenmodeRunControl,
    EigenmodeSim,
    EprAnalysisRequest,
)

sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_geometry(component)
sim.set_stack(stack)
sim.set_output_dir(Path("artifacts/aedt-xmon-eigenmode"))
sim.set_eigenmode(
    project_name="xmon_eigenmode",
    design_name="Eigenmode",
    run_control=EigenmodeRunControl(
        setup_name="Setup1",
        minimum_frequency_ghz=3.0,
        num_modes=2,
        maximum_passes=6,
        maximum_delta_frequency_percent=5.0,
    ),
    route="B",
)
sim.set_epr_request(
    EprAnalysisRequest(
        mode_indices=(1, 2),
        surface_contribution_ids=(),
        junction_ids=(),
        bulk_domain_ids=None,
    )
)
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff()
```

This request includes all configured bulk-domain outputs for modes 1 and 2; it
requests no surface-contribution or junction outputs. A surface analysis uses
`set_surface_epr(contributions=...)` with complete `SurfaceEprSpec` records
validated against the geometry catalogue, as shown by the linked handoff
example. Include a `PlanarJunction` only when its source polygon, distinct
terminal nets, direction, width, inductance, and capacitance are declared by
the source design. AEDT junctions are model elements; they are not excitation
ports. The output path must be new and unused.

### Offline Palace result example

The detached file can be moved independently of the full Palace run directory.
This analysis and ordinary Plotly export do not create a simulation object or
invoke Palace:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from scgsim.palace import reanalyze_epr, resolve_epr_result, show_epr

result = resolve_epr_result(Path("palace-eigenmode-epr.json"))
updated = reanalyze_epr(
    result,
    surface_defaults={"MA": {"loss_tangent": 2.0e-4}},
)
figure = show_epr(updated, mode=1)
figure.write_html("palace-epr-mode-1.html")
```

The AEDT counterpart uses `scgsim.aedt.resolve_epr_result(path)` and the same
module-level `reanalyze_epr(result, ...)` / `show_epr(result, mode=..., native_pass=...)` pattern. These are static API examples, not records of native solves or numerical validation.
